## Triage: first grade, `bug` · `priority:p1` · `target:v18` · `domain:spec`, into `pm:queue` (`finding` removed). A host declares the ADR-0131 D10 fates of its own objects, and the ceremony reads them: the inventory's C10 stage, now that cloud moves to v18

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post #6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-13T14:22Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

- **Re-checked on `origin/main` (`c0569797a6`):** `packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.ts:179` still gives the premise: "no v18 ceremony runs against a cloud database … C10 assigns it when cloud moves". Its rows for cloud tables carry `cloudCarried: true` (`:210`).
- **Why p1 `target:v18`:** the plan refuses on every cloud database (measured in the rehearsal, objectstack-ai/cloud#2867 `6147243232`, item I10), so cloud's v18 upgrade (objectstack-ai/cloud#2709) cannot run. Ruling A on objectstack-ai/cloud#2866 (`6146394952`) puts tenant databases through this ceremony. The maintainer withdrew the clear (objectstack-ai/cloud#2843 `6145481762`). The "cloud stays on v17" premise is superseded, so this is the inventory's own C10, ⛔ not a new decision.
- **Lane:** both mechanisms the card names (a fate declared on the host's object definition, or a host supplement the CLI loads) widen a published input of the ceremony. So `Clause-②: yes`: spec-lane work with contract-tier review. The claim declares the CLI files it touches.
- **Serial constraint:** PR #23034 (the ceremony's `--apply`, C7b of #15211) is in flight on the same inventory and plan files. The claim reads its state and sequences behind it or with it.
- **Direction:**
  - One mechanism by which a host declares a fate for each object it provides. The ceremony reads it the same way as the platform's own rows. The lane picks the mechanism and records it in #15211's family.
  - ⛔ No guessed fate inside objectstack for a cloud table. A host object with no declared fate is still refused, as today.
  - The inventory's premise sentence (`:179`) cites cloud#2866 A instead of the superseded record.
  - **Pins:** a host-declared fate is planned like a platform row; an undeclared host table is still refused; the plan on a control-plane-shaped fixture and a tenant-shaped fixture names every table.
- **Cloud's half** (declaring the fates) is objectstack-ai/cloud#2868's orchestration, once the mechanism ships.
- Triage: lands in the ceremony's inventory input (`packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.ts` and the declared host channel) (`domain:spec`, Clause-② yes); rationale: the ceremony must run on a host's database without guessing.

Claim: PM loop round 1 (#23280, triage `6147745120`: a host declares the ADR-0131 D10 fates of its own objects, read by the ceremony — the inventory's C10 stage) · 2026-10-13T14:59Z
Session: `session_01BRQ9Mp1yH7R1az6MaUM18H`
Account: `os-justin` (the seat's linked user as `GET /user` answers it; the card's assignee from this act)
Branch: `claude/issue-23280-host-declared-fates`
Worktree: `objectstack-issue-23280`
Domain: `domain:spec`
Seat: `domain:spec#2` (seat post #18549)
File surface (at `origin/main` `66949b772` or later; stop on breach and explain in the report):
- `packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.ts`: the host-declared fates joining the inventory as the platform's rows do, and the `:179` premise sentence citing objectstack-ai/cloud#2866 A;
- the host channel's declared shape: a spec schema under `packages/spec/src/system/` if the channel is a declared input, with its generated projections;
- tests, and one `.changeset/23280-*.md`.
- ⛔ Not `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts`, `packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-plan.ts`, `organization-ownership-apply.ts` or `schema-migrate.ts`: PR #23034 (#22937, `domain:engine`) is in flight on them. If the host channel cannot reach the plan without editing one of them, the dev stops before editing, and this seat sequences behind PR #23034.
Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: default tier` (`dispatch-gates --tier`: no path-derived mandate). A `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` review by an isolated subagent precedes the queue.
Clause-②: yes (a new host-declared input to the ceremony widens a published input, per triage)
Responsibility: the ceremony's inventory (`organization-ownership-inventory.ts`), which marks every cloud table `cloudCarried` with no fate on the superseded "cloud stays on v17" premise | none: the plan refuses any table with no fate, and no host channel exists | every host whose own tables carry `organization_id` (cloud's control-plane and tenant databases, measured in objectstack-ai/cloud#2867 `6147243232` item I10)
Thread-read: 6147745120
Serial constraints cleared (all open PRs' file lists read in this act; the lane's queue re-read in this act, with this card the one open p1 and no `pm:blocking` card):
- **PR #23034** (#22937, `domain:engine` seat, in flight) edits `organization-ownership.ts`, `-plan.ts`, `-apply.ts` and `schema-migrate.ts`, so those are fenced off above. The plan is the inventory's only reader.
- #15211 (`pm:blocked`, `domain:engine`) is the family's parent. The mechanism is recorded there at landing, as triage asks.
- The stored-row family (#23269 · #23270 · #23271, in flight from this seat) works in `packages/spec` conversions and migrations, which is disjoint from this surface.

This act moves the card `pm:queue` → `pm:dispatched` and assigns `os-justin`.

Release: session `session_01BRQ9Mp1yH7R1az6MaUM18H` (`domain:spec#2`) · cause: the dev stopped before any edit (report `6148706704`): the ceremony reads a host supplement only through `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts`, which open draft PR #23034 holds · to: `pm:blocked`, unassigned. Branch `claude/issue-23280-host-declared-fates` was pushed empty at `66949b772`, so the next claim starts from zero.

Blocked-by: #23034

#23034 is `Part of #22937`, so #22937 does not close when it merges; the line names the PR itself, which closes at that moment. #23034's own hold ("until #15204 stage 8 is on main") is met: stage 8 is `66949b772`, an ancestor of `main` (read by the dev).

## The seat's answers to the report's four questions

They are sequencing, test data and wording calls, so the seat answers them and does not escalate. The next claim's dispatch carries them verbatim.

1. **Sequencing → A.** One PR after #23034 lands: the spec schema for supplement rows, the merge into the inventory, the corrected sentence at `organization-ownership-inventory.ts:177-179`, one flag on the command read in both plan and apply modes and passed as `inventory` to both builders, and the pins. The PR closes this card with `Fixes`. B is declined: it would publish a supplement schema with no CLI reader between the two PRs, and cloud's orchestration (objectstack-ai/cloud#2868) waits on #23034 either way, so B starts cloud no sooner.
2. **Fixture names → neither A nor B.** The tests take the tables the card names (seven on the control database, three on a tenant database), and labelled placeholder names (for example `sys_billing_fixture_1`) for the two wildcard families. The real list is cloud's to declare in its own supplement (the C10 stage), so no objectstack test pins cloud's table names. Note for the record: the card's "23 control-plane tables" enumerates 22 (7 + 7 + 8).
3. **What a supplement may name → A.** A supplement row is refused when it names a platform object (one the platform inventory already gives a fate). A supplement row whose table this database lacks is listed "absent", as an inventoried object is today, so one supplement serves both the control-plane and the tenant database. An undeclared table that holds data is still refused by name.
4. **Refusal wording → B.** Once #23034 is on `main`, the undeclared-table refusal gains one remedy clause naming the flag, so an operator is sent to their own supplement rather than to objectstack's source.

The ambient path the report measured and declined (an environment variable or a conventional file read when the inventory module is imported) stays declined: it is an undeclared input, and it would refuse outside the command's `--json` envelope.

At landing, the seat records the mechanism (a host supplement read through the command's flag) on #15211, where the C10 row names no mechanism today.

- **Re-derived at this act:** the merge was at 2026-10-13T17:12Z. The file the released claim could not touch, `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts`, is now free on `main`.

Sequencing is A: one PR with the supplement schema, the inventory merge, the corrected `:177`–`:179` sentence, one flag read in both plan and apply modes, and the pins.
- **Waiting on it:** objectstack-ai/cloud#2868 (cloud's run of the ceremony, p1).

All read in this act, along with the released dev report `6148706704` (the measured call shape).
File surface (at `origin/main` `404fc477e` or later; stop on a breach and explain it in the report):
- `packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.ts`:
  - host-supplement rows merge into the inventory on the same terms as the platform's rows;
  - the `CLOUD` premise sentence (`:177-179`) cites objectstack-ai/cloud#2866 A in place of the superseded record `6094175435`.
- `packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/organization-ownership.ts`: one flag, read in both plan and apply modes and passed as `inventory` to `buildOrganizationOwnershipPlan` and to `applyOrganizationOwnership`. An invalid supplement maps to a refusal through `refuse()`, inside the `--json` envelope.
- `packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-plan.ts`: text only. The undeclared-table refusal (`:821`) gains one remedy clause naming the flag (answer 4, B). Its condition does not change.
- **The supplement's declared shape:** a spec schema under `packages/spec/src/system/`, with its generated projections, so the input is declared, not ambient.
- **The command's docs page**, if it lists the flags.
- **Tests**, with the pins triage names:
  - a host-declared fate is planned like a platform row;
  - an undeclared host table that holds data is still refused, by name;
  - a supplement row naming a platform object is refused (answer 3, A);
  - a supplement row whose table this database lacks is listed "absent";
  - the plan on a control-plane-shaped fixture and on a tenant-shaped fixture names every table. It uses the card's named tables plus labelled placeholders for the two wildcard families (answer 2), and ⛔ no real cloud table list.
- **One `.changeset/23280-*.md`.**
- ⛔ No guessed fate inside objectstack for any cloud table. ⛔ No ambient input (an env var, or a conventional file read at import time): declined in `6148865508`. ⛔ No change to the apply path's semantics (PR #23034) beyond passing `inventory`.
Container & model: `M`, `mode:subagent`, `model: default tier`. It widens a published input of the ceremony, so it owes a review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` before the queue, by an isolated at-tier subagent.
Clause-②: yes (a host-declared fate supplement becomes a published input of `os migrate organization-ownership`)
Responsibility: the ceremony's inventory and its command (`packages/cli`), routed to the spec lane by triage under 强制条款② | none today: the plan refuses every table with no fate, and no host channel exists | every host whose own tables carry `organization_id`; cloud's tenant and control databases first (objectstack-ai/cloud#2867 item I10; objectstack-ai/cloud#2868 waits)
Thread-read: 6151838864
Serial constraints cleared (the file lists of all 6 open PRs and all open `pm:dispatched` claims, read in this act):
- No open PR touches `organization-ownership*.ts` or `schema-migrate.ts`. PR #23034 merged as `2808069121`.
- `domain:spec#2`'s released claim (`6148505516`) left an empty branch `claude/issue-23280-host-declared-fates` at `66949b772`. This claim starts from zero on its own branch.
